maria_ml: Heads-up — trying to bring up a Mistral-derived model and our HF->Redwood convert is falling back to the slow python tokenizer. Repo has tokenizer_config.json + spm.model but no tokenizer.json, so AutoTokenizer logs 'No fast tokenizer found' and we get a PreTrainedTokenizer (slow). Batch tokenization is ~8-12x slower in our microbench. Anyone hit this before?

chris_onboard: yep, this is pretty common when the hub snapshot only includes tokenizer_config.json and sentencepiece files. Fast tokenizers rely on tokenizer.json (the tokenizers library) or a PreTrainedTokenizerFast wrapper. If tokenizer.json is missing HF falls back to slow logic.

maria_ml: Here's the exact warning from our convert run:```
/opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py:2487: UserWarning: No fast tokenizer found for this model, using slow tokenization.
  warnings.warn("No fast tokenizer found for this model, using slow tokenization.")
```

ben_platform: Short term: try `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, use_fast=True)` — sometimes HF will build a fast tokenizer from spm if the right files/classes exist. If that fails, we can generate tokenizer.json ourselves with the tokenizers library.

alex_infra: Also watch out for special tokens and config fields. tokenizer_config.json may not capture `special_tokens_map.json`, `added_tokens.json`, or padding/truncation defaults. Missing these will change tokenization and edge-case outputs (quality regressions for chat templates).

maria_ml: Right — we saw prompt truncation behave differently (padding_side/truncation_side not preserved). That caused a subtle regression in our chat evals: system prompt was partially truncated on long dialogues.

chris_onboard: Quick rebuild recipe we use:```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer, models, pre_tokenizers, decoders, processors
# load sentencepiece -> build Tokenizer then save tokenizer.json
# pseudocode: Tokenizer.from_file('spm.model') won't work; instead use tokenizers.models.SentencePieceProcessor wrapper or use sentencepiece to export vocab then build a WordPiece/BPE model...
```
If that's hairy, simpler: `tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(repo, use_fast=True); tok.save_pretrained(out_dir)` — that'll create tokenizer.json when possible.

ben_platform: I'll add an onboarding check to convert script: detect tokenizer_config.json present && tokenizer.json missing -> attempt auto-create with AutoTokenizer(use_fast=True) and if that fails, fail the conversion with a clear error and instructions. Also adding a perf smoke test (tokenization throughput) so slow fallbacks are caught early.

maria_ml: Can we also normalize special token files? Our convert currently copies tokenizer_config.json only, but doesn't assemble a special_tokens_map.json when tokens were defined in model card. That mismatch caused different token boundaries for some emoji/symbol tokens.

alex_infra: I'll put a small helper in infra: `scripts/rebuild_tokenizer.py` that tries these paths and writes out tokenizer.json + special_tokens_map.json + added_tokens.json. Will include a note in the onboarding checklist and in the model-playbook.

maria_ml: Filed INF-2345 for the regression we hit (link in PR). Also: microbench numbers — local CPU tokenization with slow fallback ~4200 tok/s vs fast ~52k tok/s at our batch sizes. That materially affects pipeline latency and worker memory pressure.

hf-bot: conversion-bot: tokenizer check completed for repo 'mistral-mini-fork' — tokenizer.json missing, attempted AutoTokenizer(use_fast=True) -> success, autogenerated tokenizer.json saved to /tmp/mistral-mini-tokenizer.json. Flagged in conversion report. :white_check_mark:

ben_platform: sweet. I'll wire the bot to attach that file to the conversion artifact and surface a warning in the Console UI when tokenizers are autogenerated.

maria_ml: thanks all — patch incoming to update convert script and onboarding doc. If anyone has a tested snippet to reliably regenerate tokenizer.json from spm + vocab + merges please drop it here.
